data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The append-only event log must require idempotency, and the published distinction is that idempotency concerns the effect of repetition on the server's intended state, while safety concerns whether the operation produces any side effects at all. In RFC 9110 terms, GET is safe (and therefore idempotent, since 'no effect' repeated is still 'no effect'), but PUT and DELETE are idempotent without being safe (they change state, but the same request repeated yields the same result). The append-only writer is analogous to PUT: it changes state (appends) but must do so idempotently so that duplicate deliveries coalesce.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the RFC 9110 definitions are not the 'published definitions' the problem intends, the analogy to PUT/DELETE may not be the intended framing.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log's append semantics do not support key-based deduplication (e.g., pure append-only with no read-before-write), idempotency must be achieved differently (e.g., client-side sequence numbers with server-side filtering).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the writer's payload includes nondeterministic content (wall-clock timestamps, random IDs), the operation cannot be made idempotent by key alone and requires a content-deterministic protocol.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110 establishes a hierarchy: all safe methods are trivially idempotent (zero effect repeated is zero effect), but not all idempotent methods are safe. PUT is the canonical example \u2014 it is idempotent (same resource state after one or many identical PUTs) but not safe (it writes to the server). The append-only log writer maps directly to this pattern: it must write (not safe) but must write idempotently (same log after one or many deliveries). The mechanism is deduplication via a deterministic operation key: the writer submits (key, payload); the log checks for an existing entry with key; if present, it returns success without appending; if absent, it appends. This makes the operation idempotent \u2014 the intended effect (log contains payload under key) is achieved regardless of how many times the delivery occurs.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
